item.title: Last SLICE Distribution & Compounding Policy
item.dc:creator: adriannico
item.content:encoded:
Intro

Exciting times are ahead of us! We’re approaching the AUXO migration and while we do so housekeeping needs to be made.

💡 If you hold, receive, or compound SLICE you may want to keep reading.

SLICE has been one of the key elements of PieDAO’s rewards distribution system, and in this article, we will explain how the SLICE distribution and the SLICE compounding processes are impacted. Let’s go!

TL;DR

Final SLICE Compounding

📅 Scheduled for April 19th.
ℹ️ SLICE sent to the Treasury after April 18th at 23:59 UTC won’t be returned

Final SLICE Distribution

📅 Scheduled for April 20th — subject to PIP-76 snapshot closing by April 18th in favor of the upgrade.
ℹ️ Eligibility criteria will set all veDOUGH holders as active to avoid slashing and enable claiming.

SLICE Compounding

As we approach the AUXO upgrade, planned Q2 2023, the termination of this service is needed as, after the migration, veDOUGH will cease to be used.

The final SLICE compounding event will be done on April 19th, 2023. Users willing to participate and convert their SLICE tokens for veDOUGH for a last time will need to send their tokens to the Treasury before that date.

⚠️ SLICE received on the Treasury after April 18th at 23:59 UTC won’t be returned

If you want to increase your veDOUGH position after this date you can redeem SLICE and trade its underlying assets on the secondary market to get more DOUGH for staking. You can still hold or transfer SLICE or its assets if you don’t.

SLICE Distribution

As per the AUXO upgrade, the rewards distribution mechanics will change. SLICE won’t be used in the AUXO DAO, as AUXO will distribute rewards in WETH. SLICE will be utilized for the last time during EPOCH#19’s rewards distribution, which will be the milestone that marks the termination of Governance Mining rewards distribution under PieDAO.

The final SLICE distribution will take place on April 20th — subject to PIP-76 snapshot closing by April 18th in favor of the upgrade.

Claiming and redeeming SLICE after the migration

veDOUGH holders will still be able to CLAIM their SLICE rewards anytime after final the distribution is complete. All addresses in the final merkle tree will be entitled to do so, regardless of whether they migrated their locks (or not) to the AUXO products.

ℹ️ After the AUXO upgrade, users can continue to use the legacy PieDAO website to claim and redeem SLICE or any other PieDAO product

PieDAO Legacy sites

  • For SLICE, BCP, PLAY, DeFi++ go to https://piedaoorg.netlify.app/
  • For older decommissioned products and Farms can go to https://legacy.auxo.fi/

Last SLICE Distribution & Compounding Policy was originally published in PieDAO on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: Everything you need to know about migrating veDOUGH to AUXO
item.dc:creator: adriannico
item.content:encoded:
Intro

The DAO seeks to upgrade its business model and services by introducing the Auxo. Auxo DAO will focus on multi-chain treasury farming while seeking to develop Lending and Bonding offerings. The upgrade aims to establish a new brand and make the DAO more vibrant, sustainable, efficient, and scalable. This brings new products to the table, as DOUGH, veDOUGH, eDOUGH, and all the PIEs will no longer be maintained.

🚨 veDOUGH holders, attention! Your action is required to migrate your locks. This article will seek to describe the process and options, so don’t panic.

Ready? Let’s get warm up the engines to enter this exciting new era, the AuxoDAO era!

[TL;DR]

  • The migration window has been planned from April 19th, to May 19th.
  • veDOUGH locks can be migrated to ARV (Active Rewards Vault) and/or PRV (Passive Rewards Vault).
  • Choose ARV for greater rewards and active governance. Choose PRV for fewer rewards, passive governance, and transferability.
  • AUXO products support one lock per address for ARV.
  • Individual locks can be migrated to different addresses — Restrictions may apply
  • All non-migrated veDOUGH will be unlocked after the migration’s end.
  • DOUGH buyback will run for 1-week post migration — Subject to funds availability

The Migration

Let’s first set some definitions in place:

  • User: veDOUGH holders
  • Migration: the process of transferring user locks from PieDAO’s system to AuxoDAO.
  • Migration Window: The designated period of time when the interface will allow users to migrate. It has a start and end date, and actions can only take place within that range.
  • The Window: Planned to Starts on April 19th | Ends on May 19th

User Paths

Users will have two main paths to take, it’s critical that you define if you want to MIGRATE or STAY.

| Users MIGRATING | Will need to take action during the migration window in order to migrate your locks to the new Auxo protocol. The interface wizard will guide you through the process of choosing between ARV (Active Rewards Vault) or PRV (Passive Rewards Vault) and offer you the possibility to migrate locks individually (one by one) or aggregate them (merge all into one).

| Users Staying | Will be able to unstake and claim your DOUGH after the migration window ends and the tokens are unlocked. Each position is locked and they’ll need to be unstaked individually. You can review and unstake here.

Accrued SLICE will be claimable by the receiving address, regardless if veDOUGH locks were migrated or unlocked.

The Products

In this section, we will differentiate how each protocol handles its token locks and the difference between each product.

DOUGH locks vs AUXO locks

The migration of DOUGH locks will introduce significant changes in how locks will be managed. Staking AUXO will create single-lock positions, simplifying position management for users.

  1. Every time DOUGH is staked, a new lock is created, which has its own start date, end date, and length.
  2. When AUXO is staked a lock is created with its own start date, end date, and length, but the main differences are:
    (a) Every new AUXO staked under the same address will not create a new lock: it will increase the current lock’s position and restart the staking time.

The Auxo DAO Products

  • The Active Rewards Vault
    | ARV | is a non-transferable asset that will allow you to get monthly rewards for governing the DAO. It receives more rewards, can be redeemed for AUXO after the lock expiration, and has the option to exit to PRV by paying a 20% early lock termination fee. 70% of the Treasury Farming will be distributed monthly as rewards to active holders (who voted during the previous month). The amount will be subject to a level system that boosts the rewards of those with longer expiration dates — levels decay on a monthly basis, and should be boosted monthly to maximize the rewards received.
  • The Passive Rewards Vault
    | PRV | Is a transferable asset that will allow you to get monthly rewards for stabilising the Auxo price while being free from governance obligations. PRV requires to be staked to receive rewards and can be unstaked anytime. 30% of the Treasury Farming will be distributed monthly as rewards to its holders who staked. The ARV→PRV conversion is irreversible, but PRV can be withdrawn for AUXO (subject to budget availability and a fee).

What to migrate to — In a nutshell

  • | Choose ARV | if you are willing to commit to active governance while receiving the highest possible returns (rewards).
  • | Choose PRV | if you are willing to be passive on governance by holding a governance-free and transferable asset.
Deep dive and compare each product through the following articles
📽️ >> Options for veDOUGH
📝 >> The Active Rewards Vault
📝 >> The Passive Rewards Vault
📝 >> Rewards Vault Comparison

Lock Mechanics

Impact on the lock’s length

There are two scenarios that need to be outlined in order to understand how DOUGH locks migration will impact the AUXO locks length (this applies to ARV and PRV):

  • | Boosting: Your new AUXO lock will be set to the max length (36 months) as well as rewards level (level 30) if migrated to ARV. The lock start date will be reset to the day you migrate.
  • | Not Boosting: Your new lock duration will be determined by the remaining time to expiration of your DOUGH lock (or the longest one if you are aggregating). If your time to expiration is lower than the minimum (6 months), then the minimum lock time will be applied
Examples
1️⃣ John has 2 DOUGH locks with 2 different expiration dates (lock A expires in 10 months and lock B expires in 34 months). John chooses to migrate and boost today. His AUXO lock will start today and expire in 36 months — The amount of ARV received will be equal to staking AUXO for 36 months
2️⃣ John has 2 DOUGH locks with 2 different expiration dates (lock A expires in 10 months and lock B expires in 34 months). John chooses to migrate without boosting today. His AUXO lock start will today and expires in 34 months — The amount of ARV received will be equal to staking AUXO for 34 months
3️⃣ John has 2 DOUGH locks with 2 different expiration dates (lock A expires in 3 months and lock B expires in 5 months). John chooses to migrate without boosting today. His AUXO lock start will be today and expires in 6 months — The amount of ARV received will be equal to staking AUXO for 6 months.

Conversion Ratio

The migration is about moving your locked DOUGH to AUXO, and then staking AUXO for either ARV or PRV. During that process, there’re three ratios that apply:

  • | DOUGH:AUXO ratio | The DOUGH to AUXO conversion is set at 100:1. This has been set in order to define the AUXO supply and to factor in the DOUGH supply after completing the burning of the Treasury-owned DOUGH.
  • | AUXO:ARV ratio | The amount of ARV received by staking AUXO is determined by two elements: the locked amount and the time commitment (6 to 36 months), following the curve: y=x/k*log(x) — the same mechanic that DOUGH:veDOUGH had.
  • | AUXO:PRV ratio | The AUXO:PRV ratio is 1:1, as no curve or decay applies.

Possible Combinations

Final considerations

  • Migrating is a one-time opportunity. Once it ends, it’s over.
  • You can exercise governance from the moment you receive ARV.
  • Remember to stake your PRV in order to receive rewards.
  • If you did not migrate, you’ll still be able to unstake your DOUGH once unlocked at PieDAO’s website.
  • The final DOUGH buyback epoch (Epoch#10) will start after migration is over and last for 1 week, subject to funds availability — Buyback page

Everything you need to know about migrating veDOUGH to AUXO was originally published in PieDAO on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: The AUXO Upgrade
item.dc:creator: adriannico
item.content:encoded:
About this doc

Hello, anon! 👋 We will explain to you in this document all about the PieDAO-to-AuxoDAO upgrade in order to give you enough context, visibility, and tools to play your cards properly.

⚠️READ ME: Details disclosed in this post are sensitive and subject to change during the course of the migration. Changes may include but are not limited to, adding decay functions, changing the staking options, updating timelines, and scope modifications.

Table of Contents

  • The Story: Why are we Upgrading?
  • The Roadmap: What’s the plan?
  • The Upgrade Impact: What changes?
  • The User Paths: What you need to know and do

The Story

As you may have heard, the Index business has put the DAO in a position where it was operating at loss, mostly due to the fact that there’s limited market fit for Index products (a.k.a. PIEs ❤️) within the Crypto Ecosystem. As highlighted in the ‘Time to say Good Pie’ post from Alexintosh, this is mostly due to a lack of market interest, and technical limitations on building and maintaining pies impacting their scalability, costs, and revenue model.

The core team has been exploring ideas and building tech to develop new offerings that allow bringing value to our community (DAO members). The Governance Mining initiative, where users stake the DAO token $Dough to get rewards from treasury farming operations through active governance, has been chosen as the service offering base — considering its performance during its 1st year of operations. The proposals that follow and the core goal of the upgrade are to make the DAO sustainable, efficient, and scalable.

A new service needed a new name: so AuxoDAO was born. Rebranding was a necessary move, as food-branded protocols fashion seemed to have faded away.

Auxo will focus on multi-chain treasury farming, with yields going to veAUXO stakers. Liquidity will be protocol owned, with the goal to keep the value aligned with the NAV of the treasury without selling pressure from incentives. As explained by Alexintosh in his ‘The Raise of Auxo’ post, where the brand was introduced:

AuxoDAO is fundamentally different from PieDAO because veAUXO holders administer DAO-owned funds with the mandate of generating yield, compared to creating and managing tokenized funds that use yield strategies for others.

In the following articles we will describe the key aspects, changes, and activities, so keep reading 😊.

If you still need more context the following links will be quite useful (in order of appearance):

  • Doughpamine programme termination
  • Time to say Good Pie
  • Dough/eDough Buyback
  • The Rise of Auxo
  • Treasury Dough Burning

The Roadmap

Any initiative needs a plan and every plan a timeline. The PieDAO→ AuxoDAO upgrade activities have already started, and the community support has been formalized by the recently passed vote: [Gate 1] Auxo Migration. In this article, you’ll find the milestones and their timelines.

>>> Go to the article

The Upgrade Impact

As per Newton’s third law of motion, there’s a reaction for every action. The DAO upgrade will be making considerable changes at the protocol layer, upgrading its governance mechanics, treasury management participation, product and service offerings, and branding. In the following article, we will be digging deeper into introduced changes.

>>> Go to the article

The User Paths

Users can choose to be part of the upgrade or not. In this piece we define the roads each one can decide to walk, focusing on Dough, veDough, and eDough holders.

>>> Go to the article

item.dc:creator: adriannico
item.content:encoded:
>>> Go back to the main article: The Auxo Upgrade

⚠️READ ME: Details disclosed in this post are sensitive and subject to change during the course of the migration. Changes may include but are not limited to, adding decay functions, changing the staking options, updating timelines, and scope modifications.

Users Upgrading

Are you upgrading? Great, you’ll be more than welcome in AuxoDAO, here’s what you need to know.

  • Dough won’t be upgraded to Auxo, veAuxo, or xAuxo. If you are willing to upgrade, you’ll need to stake it.
  • eDough won’t be upgraded to Auxo, veAuxo or xAuxo. If you are willing to upgrade, you’ll need to bridge it — bridging is available only if the vesting period is higher than 6 months.
  • veDough won’t be bridged automatically. You will be asked to upgrade to veAuxo or xAuxo through an interface during April 2023.
⚠️veDOUGH holders who don’t take action to upgrade within the 3 months window won’t be able to do so in the future. After this deadline, all veDOUGH locks will be nulled.

Users Not Upgrading

Are you choosing to exit? We’ll miss you anon, thanks for the moments shared, and good luck! By the way, here’s what you need to know:

  • Dough holders can hold, sell or burn their tokens. Selling can happen in the open market or through the BuyBack program (no slippage). Know more about the buyback here. Giga chads willing to burn can do it here.
  • eDough holders can keep vesting, burn, or sell them. Selling can happen through the BuyBack program (no minimum vesting time required). Giga chads willing to burn can do it here.
  • veDough can be held until the upgrade date, and if not upgraded it will be unlocked and ready for you to claim here.
⚠️Be mindful that the Dough and eDough buyback program will be terminated on March 20th, 2023.

item.title: The Upgrade Impact
item.dc:creator: adriannico
item.content:encoded:
>>> Go back to the main article: The Auxo Upgrade

⚠️READ ME: Details disclosed in this post are sensitive and subject to change during the course of the migration. Changes may include but are not limited to, adding decay functions, changing the staking options, updating timelines, and scope modifications.

On Staking

Main changes introduced

  • Enable on-chain governance and delegation: Governance now will be on-chain enabled, allowing for greater decentralization and greater control of the veAUXO holders.
  • Protocol native Liquid staking: Native liquid staking functionality for xAUXO holders that opt-in to trade off rewards and voting power over liquid holdings.
  • Aggregation of all locks into a single position: Easier and more cost-efficient staking management for the user and the DAO.

Before and After Models Comparison

veAUXO vs xAUXO Comparison

On Treasury Management

The Auxo governance will increase the degree of control that veAUXO holders have over treasury operations. veAUXO holders will be able to:

  • Whitelist contracts and signatures
  • Whitelist Operators

This is possible via on-chain voting, allowing veAUXO holders to whitelist contract addresses and contract signatures through transparent governance.

On Governance

In AuxoDAO governance is designed around the resilience of operation and keeps the system trustless and decentralized. veAUXO holders serve different roles including but not limited to:

  • Notarization & Transparency: Community voting is used as a subjective oracle to insure full transparency about how strategies are performing, together with information about how they’re set up, operated, and composed.
  • Authorization and Access Control: veAUXO holders control the authorization layer of the Treasury by whitelisting contract addresses and contract signatures. This system allows only authorized transactions are executed by Treasury operators.
  • Election of Treasury Operators: veAUXO holders can add and remove Treasury Operators at any time, decreasing operational risks and expanding governance capabilities.
  • Issuing Liquidity Events: veAUXO holders have veto power to authorize or block new liquidity events.

On Products and Services

item.title: Delivering Rewarding Governance Mechanisms For DAOs
item.dc:creator: bayraqi
item.content:encoded:
Ever wondered how to improve the quality of governance of your DAO? Are you struggling to align the DAO to its mandate? PieDAO has implemented a solution that rewards members for participating in the DAO’s governance matters.

TL;DR

  • The rewards distribution mechanism distributes 60% of the total treasury’s farming monthly earnings.
  • The eligibility criteria reward those holders that are actively contributing to governance while redistributing the rewards from those who don’t.
  • Staking veDough and voting at least once a month are the minimum requirements to participate.

Background

A proposal known as PIP-60, published on August 27th, 2021, fundamentally changed how PieDAO would operationalize a value accrual mechanism for token holders that attract long-term capital by rewarding active participation in the DAO. The staking framework used by the DAO distributes protocol fees and other revenues the organization generates.

The proposal also defined the DAO’s revenues and the distribution breakdown that allocates 60% directly to veDOUGH holders, 25% towards compounding the treasury principal, and the remainder to cover operational costs.

Now that you are hooked on the pie, let’s see how the process transpires.

Players

There are three leading players to consider in the process:

  • Treasury Farming Committee — this body determines the number of tokens that will be made available for distribution at month-end.
  • Core contributors — core operators of the rewards system are responsible for issuing monthly reports, issuing the rewards distribution and minting SLICE (the PieDAO reward token).
  • veDOUGH holders — members who validate issued reports and notarize the distribution amounts and recipients.

Defining The Distribution Amounts

At the end of the month, the treasury farming committee issues the farming reports that disclose the amounts earned by the treasury marked for distribution and to be used for minting SLICE. The allocated portion is sent to a multi-sig controlled by the core contributors for the monthly distribution.

The SLICE is a basket of top-performing crypto-assets managed by PieDAO, whose composition is defined through governance voting. This opportunity provides an exposure-as-a-service function as veDOUGH holders vote to change the composition of the rewards to a most beneficial position. This is similar to dollar-cost averaging into a portfolio of assets over time, but the assets are governance-managed and community picked.

Operations

SLICE is minted once the assets for distribution are defined and transferred to the core contributors, who generate reports that detail the tokens to be allocated to every qualified recipient. This opens a 72-hour snapshot period where you, as a DOUGH holder, are required to review and verify that your address and rewards balance are reflecting correctly on the Merkle tree shared by the core contributors.

The review has to happen during a 72h notarization window, where veDough holders will be required to vote if the merkle tree is valid or not — the notarization process supporting documentation is always shared in the snapshot vote, so there is no need for you to remember the process.

Eligibility

The following can be used to determine eligibility:

  • If you voted in the last epoch, you are eligible. Your rewards will accumulate in your account and you will be able to claim them when distributed.
  • If you did not vote in the last epoch but voted in the earlier epoch, you are also eligible but flagged as inactive. The rewards will accumulate in your account, however, you will not be able to claim them as the claimable balance is determined as zero as per being inactive.
  • If you haven’t voted in 3 consecutive months your unclaimed rewards will be redistributed (slashed) among all eligible members. After slashing, the holder’s unclaimed balance will be equal to zero.

- Eligibility is determined by whether you voted or not during last month’s voting period(referred to as an epoch).

- Accumulation means that the allocated rewards will accrue to your account and will reflect in your account balance.

- Claiming will be the ability to withdraw the accumulated balance.

Notarization

Once you assess your eligibility, you can approach the notarization process and approve the distribution details in the report. Ensure that you can locate your address in the Merkle tree and check the rewards to be distributed to your account (remember the balance show the cumulative position that lists all unclaimed assets)

If your account is missing or there seems to be an error with your allocation, kindly vote as invalid and alert the core dev team at the DAO to look into your matter whilst the snapshot is still open — at the #bug-report channel at PieDAO’s discord

Please note that the claiming process is suspended whilst the snapshot is running and you can only resume claiming once the snapshot has been concluded and the distribution completed.

Distribution

Once the snapshot vote has been concluded, the rewards are distributed to your account. A message will be shared on the official channels to inform about the distribution. If you decide to claim your SLICE you’ll be able to redeem, accumulate or forward your balance for further compounding. If you don’t want to claim, that’s also fine, you will keep accruing rewards as long are you don’t get slashed

Worth mentioning that you can compound your SLICE for more veDough to increase your position. If you choose this option you will be claiming your SLICE and sending it to the PieDAO Treasury’s address, which will define a rate and distribute the veDough 2 weeks after the distribution happens — now more about the mechanism here.

Happy days, eh?

You Want In?

If you want to get some Dough you can swap if for ETH at Sushiswap or 1Inch. Then proceed to the Staking Portal to stake your Dough, or to the Staking Simulator tool to simulate the amount of veDOUGH (vote-escrowed DOUGH) you can earn for a determined lock-up period.

Conclusion

Every month, a new distribution will come where the treasury committee and the core contributors team handle the asset allocation and rewards distribution. It is your duty as a veDOUGH holder to support through validation during this process and to participate in Governance not only to get rewards but to also build and grow the DAO. Keep voting!!

Remember to join the Discord community and follow the DAO’s official communication channels listed on the website. Also, read about the first DAO-to-DAO acquisition in Ethereum’s history.

Happy staking and earning!

item.title: BDI: The Phantom Migration
item.dc:creator: adriannico
item.content:encoded:
We went 🐳 hunting and we came back empty-handed 😕, do you want to know why? In this article, we will explain the outcome of the BasketDAO acquisition, as a retrospective for this DAO-2-DAO acquisition experiment.

A Quick Recap

In October 2021 BasketDAO suffered exploits that impacted their users significantly. The BasketDAO treasury funds were destined to compensate the holders but ultimately lead to the products and community collapse. Their core dev team sadly decided to wind down operations and were looking for mechanisms to take care of their members and holders while doing so. Here’s where PieDAO comes into the picture, where jointly worked to offer an elegant exit to holders who wanted to stay invested in Defi index products and a DAO community while migrating away from BasketDAO (read all about it here). Teams have worked together to build a migration, draft a strategy and communicate it to their communities and in this article, we cover the results of such efforts.

A migration for BDI holders (BasketDAO’s Defi exposure index) where a 3-week migration window was defined which ends today (Jul 21st, 2022) where BasketDAO BDI holders could migrate to PieDAO’s DEFI++ token.

Its success was deeply tied to the participation of BDI holders to opt-in and the BasketDAO community support…and you guessed: that did not happen. Keep reading to know why.

We imagined a world where we

  • Allowed BDI holders to keep DFI ecosystem exposure through a liquid and maintained product
  • Onboarded the BasketDAO community into PieDAO
  • Migrated to PieDAO of the residual TVL in $BDI, BasketDAO’s DEFI Index (~$1.76M as of April 25th, 2022)
  • Offered to mint and distribute KPI Options as rewards for those who hold the migrated liquidity for 12 months if at least 50% of the current BDI tokens were deposited.
  • Enabled BDI holders who migrate to participate in PieDAO’s Governance Mining initiative
  • Could leverage on the BasketDAO team to reach major bag holders and get them onboard

But not all dreams come true

⛔ Developed a contract to carry out the migration transparently. Only 7 deposits were recorded.

⛔ Engaged with the BasketDAO community on Discord and Twitter. No response nor interest was shown.

⛔ Distributed NFTs to communicate to large holders about the initiative so that we could reach the 50% BDI tokens threshold. Whales burned tokens instead.

⛔ Prepared the KPI Options parameters with the UMA tech team to be ready to launch. We did not reach the min deposit amount, so we won’t proceed with the KPI Options or veDough distribution.

Outcome

Did the migration fail? Yes, as it did not meet the objectives. Yet, we died trying 💪.

  • We expected a potential capital inflow of ~$1.76M to boost DEFI++ TVL and got ~$42.4K (2.4%). We hardly cover the time and resources put into this task.
  • We expected a min of ~4372 tokens deposited to mint the KPI Options and got ~402 (9%). This results in the cancellation of the KPI Options distribution
  • We expected to leverage the BasketDAO community to participate and help spread the news… it proved to be dead ☠️. We still welcome their members but will cease efforts to pursue their engagement.

Lessons learned

We took a lot of lessons learned with us, which we’d like to share with anyone approaching a DAO-2-DAO acquisition in the future

  1. If you plan to leverage any community to manage media outreach and participation first assess their interest and check its heartbeat signs (spoiler: dead means dead)
  2. Secure whales participation or any critical participant before taking any action
  3. Assess that there’s interest in what you are giving in return
  4. Invest time only if you can have a few metrics that anticipate min success, otherwise, you’ll be subject to the whims of fate.

The first point is quite important, so let’s dig deeper

In Web2, companies maintain ownership of extensive user data and contact lists. While this has raised extensive privacy concerns over the years, one major benefit is that it allows important communications to be very easily spread to users.
You don’t have that in Web3, as we found.
You typically have:
- A wallet address
- A discord/telegram server
- A webpage
If your discord/telegram is dead, and nobody is visiting your webpage, your reach is severely limited.
Airdropping NFTs had some impact for us, but not the impact we wanted.
What we learned was how important it is to be able to reach your users, even if they have disengaged, and have contingencies in place if your main channels do not work.

Next steps

It’s the end. Deposited funds will be available to be withdrawn once the migration is complete, so holders can get their DEFI++ tokens in return. As mentioned before, KPI Options won’t be minted as min threshold has not been met, so no further efforts are required on that front.

So, the next steps are:

  • Migrating the BDI tokens to DEFI++ (to be announced at PieDAO’s discord channel)
  • Enable withdrawals in the migration app

Conclusion

We should label this as an Acquisition of Knowledge. Even though the results were not as expected the whole web3 ecosystem is about experimentation, and that’s what we did and will gladly keep doing.

We appreciate everyone that participated on both ends, has been a long and fun ride.

item.title: PieDAO acquires BasketDAO, welcome to the family!
item.dc:creator: adriannico
item.content:encoded:
This deal is one of the first DAO-to-DAO acquisitions in Ethereum’s history. PieDAO to boost its user base and DeFi token TVL.

TL;DR

  • BasketDAO wound down its operations on October 22nd, 2021 following an exploit.
  • The BasketDAO core team reached out to PieDAO to discuss a partnership. The partnership allows Basket DAO Index (BDI) holders to migrate liquidity into PieDAO.
  • As a result of the acquisition, BDI holders have the option to swap for PieDAO’s DeFi token. BDI holders will be able to migrate from June 29th to July 21st.
  • Those who migrate liquidity can also receive BDI-DeFi KPI Options (powered by UMA). At expiry, the BDI-DeFi KPI Options can be redeemed for PieDAO’s governance token veDOUGH.
  • The awarded veDOUGH will have a 6-month lockup period during which it’ll earn governance mining rewards.

Table of contents

  • 👥 Participating parties
  • 🧐 Some background
  • 🗳️ The proposal
  • 🧭The Migration and the KPI Options
  • 📅 Timeline
  • 📝Conclusion

👥 Participating parties

The acquisition is between two DAOs in the crypto indices space on Ethereum:

  • PieDAO is a user-owned community that provides mechanisms that aim to generate wealth. It was the first to propose crypto index products (known as PIEs).
  • BasketDAO was a protocol that offered yield-bearing crypto indices powered by Yearn. Their products targeted long-term passive investors with features such as no management fees.

At the core, both projects have a similar goal: offering products that allow users to capture the wealth crypto is creating. The similarities don’t stop there. For example, BasketDAO’s flagship token BDI is conceptually a PieVault. As a reminder, PieVaults allow for lending, staking, and yield-farming of underlying assets. This natural fit between both projects allowed acquisition talks to move quickly.

🧐 Some background

On October 22nd, 2021 the BasketDAO team received a message alerting them to unusual activity. An investigation ensued which allowed for the core team to discover the exploit. The attacker stole BDI tokens by taking advantage of a vulnerability in a contract. The attacker subsequently washed the stolen funds through Tornado Cash.

Following the exploit, BasketDAO took actions aimed at compensating the victims. First, they distributed available treasury fees to the victims. They then removed exit fees from their contracts. And finally organized social burnings for users who wanted to exit their positions.

At some point during all this, the BasketDAO team decided to step away from the project. Not wanting to abandon their users with illiquid tokens they searched for alternatives. This is when talks between the BasketDAO and PieDAO teams began.

As mentioned before the talks progressed quickly. PieDAO had an interest in similar projects and this was no different. In PieDAO’s view, although they were competitors any innovation in this early space was to be celebrated. So when the BasketDAO team reached out about acquiring we jumped at the opportunity.

🗳️ The proposal

The passed proposal provides a migration option for BDI holders. BDI holders will be able to deposit their tokens into the mixer and exchange them for our DeFi token.

Our DeFi token is a streamlined version of BDI. It holds fourteen different DeFi tokens to BDI’s seventeen. Don’t worry! We cover the major players- Maker, Uniswap, Aave, Link, etc. and only differ in the low market cap projects. Why is there a difference in low market cap token inclusion? We’ve found that a lack of token liquidity can affect our scaling potential so we decided to be selective.

As mentioned before DeFi uses our PieVault architecture. This allows for lending, staking, and yield-farming of underlying assets for additional growth. Best of all, there is no withdrawal fee. And a competitive 0.7% streaming fee towards veDOUGH holders (more on that later!).

Now back to the proposal. A BDI holder (let’s say you) has three weeks to deposit your BDI tokens into the mixer. After the deposit window closes our mixer will start blending the tokens. During that phase, no action will be necessary from your end. At this point, everyone who deposited will receive BDI-DeFi KPI Options. Once mixing is complete you are free to withdraw your DeFi tokens OR keep them in the mixer for 12 months.

Why would you lock your tokens away for 12 months? Well, here’s where it gets exciting. Remember the BDI-DeFi KPI Options you received earlier? After expiry the options turn into veDOUGH, our governance token. This turns you into a full-time member and owner of our DAO. Apart from voting rights veDOUGH confers other perks which might be worth your while. There is a caveat though, at least +50% of the DeFi deposited must remain in the contract for the entire year. Otherwise, the options will be worth nothing. So we encourage all incoming BasketDAO members to stick with us!

Highlights

  1. Migration to PieDAO of the residual TVL in $BDI, BasketDAO’s DeFi Index 3 (~$1.76M*)
  2. Onboarding of the BasketDAO community into PieDAO

*all figures as of April 25th 2022

🧭Migration and the BDI-KPI Options

The Migration

BDI holders will have a 3 week migration window to deposit their BDI tokens (Open: Jun 29th | Close: Jul 21st), getting DeFi++ in return.

If you want to participate in this migration, go to basketdao.org and deposit your BDI tokens. The tokens will be deposited in a migration contract (mixer) that will manage the process in 3 phases.

  • Phase 0 | Target: Deposits Open — Ready to receive BDI tokens and account for deposits.
  • Phase 1 | Target: Deposits Closed — No more deposits accepted, gov multisig will mix the DEFI++ tokens and set the exchange rate.
  • Phase 2 | Target: Withdrawal Open — Withdrawals are open and users should be able to withdraw their corresponding DEFI++.

BDI-DeFi KPI Options in depth

Once deposits are closed we’ll record (via snapshot) the total balance of tokens migrated per address. The BDI-DeFi KPI Options will then be minted and available to participating addresses. An expiration date for the options will be set for 12 months from minting.

At expiration, the KPI Options will settle. KPI options will be worth zero unless +50% of the DeFi tokens remain in the contract. We will use the snapshot to confirm balance.

PieDAO to offer BDI holders a conversion through KPI options tokens, powered by UMA

  1. The BDI-DeFi KPI Options nominal max payout corresponds to the current BASK Circulating Market Cap as of April 25th 2022 [ → $91,222]
  2. KPI options to veDOUGH conversion: The options will be collateralized by DOUGH with a nominal max payout as defined above. They will be converted to veDOUGH, according to its 30days avg price as of April 25th 2022 [ → $0.2153, resulting in an equivalent max payout of 423,674 DOUGH]. The resulting DOUGH at KPI conversion will then be converted to veDOUGH, with a time-lock of 6 months, during which holders receive Governance Mining Rewards.
  3. The KPI Options will expire 12 months after distribution.

KPI measured (chart below)

  1. Proportional to the stickiness (% of the liquidity in the contract at the time of expiration against the total deposits) of BDI Liquidity migrated.
  2. A minimum of 50% of migrated liquidity should be sticky at conversion for KPI Options to convert to a non-zero value.
  3. Liquidity will be tracked resulting in “DEFI++” units after migration, corresponding to the BDI liquidity deposited by holders in the migration contract.

📅 Timeline

  • PieDAO governance vote complete | May 11th, 2022
  • Migration contract deployment | May 23rd, 2022
  • Migration dates| Open: Jun 29th, 2022 / Close: Jul 21st, 2022
  • KPI Options: Snapshot taken | Target date: Jul 21st, 2022
  • KPI Options mint day | Target date to be announced at PieDAO’s discord
  • Options expiration | 12 months from Options mint date

📝Conclusion

Wow, that was a long read. We’d like to close this read with a few insights that are worth noting:

  • 💯 This is the first DAO-to-DAO acquisition! Driven by the will to give fellow DeFi believers a second chance 🤝
  • 👪 ****We want you as part of the family! 💕 +98% of the PieDAO community was in favor of the proposal
  • 🧩 Process transparency built on top of a battle-tested DeFi lego block: UMA KPI Options
  • ⛏️ Holders’ will be awarded veDOUGH, PieDAO’s governance token, earning Governance Mining rewards during its 6-month lock period.

Thanks for your support, stay crusty 🥧

Special thanks to our members Bntez and kitblake for your collaboration writing this article 👏

PieDAO acquires BasketDAO, welcome to the family! was originally published in PieDAO on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: Investing in the Metaverse with PieDAO
item.dc:creator: Bntez
item.content:encoded:
PieDAO’s $PLAY product is tailored for those who are looking for diversified exposure to the blue-chips of metaverse and gaming

This article appeared in The McNeill Report and has been published here with permission.

PieDAO is an asset-allocation DAO that builds and maintains financial products so that anyone can obtain exposure to the sector of their choice in a diversified manner. Since inception, they have consistently built and maintained products that remove a lot of the headaches from speculating on investments in the cryptocurrency arena. The community has experienced great success in this endeavour thus far, leveraging the inherent flexibility of DAOs to make a variety of different product offerings and find innovative ways to generate more yield for holders of PieDAO products, as well as pioneering industry-leading infrastructure for combatting voter apathy and ensuring that holders of PieDAO’s governance token are adequately remunerated for their contributions (with a specific focus on output rather than input).

Different DAOs across the DeFi space are currently experimenting with ways in which revenue can be distributed amongst governance holders. As Ethereum and DAOs dematerialise traditional work environments (particularly those that don’t require physically-taxing manual labour), it has become clear that this is not an easy issue to contend with, and many projects have had a varied focus on the best way to fairly and efficiently reward their communities for their contributions.

I have not found a more compelling example of how DeFi governance can be properly incentivised than PieDAO’s example. The structure currently in place means that governance token holders can share in DAO revenues if they pledge their allegiance to the DAO for a certain period of time by staking for ve-tokens, and vote on governance proposals.

The theory behind these innovations, which were implemented in October 2021, was that this would mitigate the risk of mercenary capital and ensure that PieDAO could depend upon a community with incentives sustained over the long term. In practice, what this meant was that PieDAO dramatically exceeded expectations and became one of the most active DAOs (if not the most active DAO) in the crypto space.

alexintosh.eth | I'm hiring on Twitter: "DAOs are communities first, the relevant metrics are first and foremost related to participation.veDOUGH tackles a hard problem in most DAOs today: Governance free-riding and voting apathy.With a participation rate of 68.26% @PieDAO_DeFi is among the most active Ethereum DAO. https://t.co/H7plznyDhK / Twitter"

DAOs are communities first, the relevant metrics are first and foremost related to participation.veDOUGH tackles a hard problem in most DAOs today: Governance free-riding and voting apathy.With a participation rate of 68.26% @PieDAO_DeFi is among the most active Ethereum DAO. https://t.co/H7plznyDhK

To understand the significance of this pragmatically, it is only useful to compare PieDAO with other DAOs to a certain extent. Since most of the world’s capital currently resides outside cryptocurrencies, it is more useful to compare these statistics with those in traditional finance. As a capital allocation DAO, the main roles of the PieDAO’s veDOUGH holders are to ensure that the DAOs products are well-managed. This process includes rebalancing, which assets to include in indexes (PIP-59), establishing remuneration for governance (PIP-64), and protecting investors from security concerns (PIP-66), etc. Since October, when the current structure for remunerating governance token holders was implemented, the number of voting wallets has risen to 392 (as of the time of writing). There are currently five indexes (or “pies”) that are actively managed by the DAO: PLAY, DeFi+S, DeFi+L, DeFi++ and BCP. When one considers that BCP is simply an amalgamation of WBTC, ETH, and DeFi++, and that DeFi+S and DeFi+L are to be deprecated into DeFi++ as part of the DAO’s product refinement initiative, it becomes apparent that there are 392 wallets that are focused on ensuring that the PLAY and DeFi++ pies are managed as efficiently as possible.

To put this into context, there is no fund manager in the world that has this many people overseeing this many funds, and certainly not with the combined wisdom that comes with a DAO’s hive mind. No matter how adept an individual may be at their craft, they will struggle to compete against hundreds of other people who are attempting to achieve the same.

Compared to many other funds, especially those in DeFi (which often have a higher barrier to entry, particularly for institutions), the fees on PieDAO’s indexes are also comparatively low: fees range from 0.7%-1% depending on whether or not further strategies are being employed to generate yield and to which extent. For example, some pies will generate yield on the assets within the indexes by lending them out automatically and in a gas-efficient manner (pooling assets with several others into a pie is a hugely efficient method of achieving this). This strategy is particularly noticeable in DeFi+L, and will be rolled out to $PLAY as soon as it is deemed feasible.

So what is $PLAY ?

$PLAY is PieDAO’s product offering that allows people to automatically and seamlessly invest into the largest projects in metaverse and gaming. Currently, the index consists of MANA, SAND, AXS, ILV, ENJ, GALA, AUDIO and YGG.

MANA

One of the longest-running metaverses, and certainly one of the largest, is Decentraland. MANA operates as the in-game currency for this metaverse (wearables and virtual real estate is priced in MANA), as well as the governance token for the Decentraland DAO, which oversees the governance of the ecosystem. For this reason, amongst others, Decentraland is often touted as the most decentralised metaverse that exists — for this reason it has already gained large-scale institutional support such as those who are invested in MANA through the Grayscale fund. In terms of metaverses (and it is quite possible in the future that there will be thousands), Decentraland is by far the most revered amongst OGs and has the most proven track record over time.

As well as the in-game currency, MANA token holders will have the ability to vote on the ways in which LAND (the NFTs that constitute the Decentraland metaverse) and estates can be upgraded, the ways in which LAND can be auctioned in the future, marketplace fees (always denominated in MANA — some of which gets burned), allocation of MANA for grants and development efforts, voting to replace and manage the security council, etc.

SAND

SAND has exploded into prominence recently due to the high-quality graphics of their metaverse and the extra utility that is afforded to holders. The Sandbox, so named due to the lack of constraints that exist within virtual worlds, has been pioneering in many ways that their competitors have not, such as focusing on the integration of NFTs which are external to the platform as avatars.

AXS

Axie Infinity was one of the best-performing assets in the metaverse and gaming space in 2021, largely credited with bringing play-to-earn mechanics to the fore. The ramifications for such game mechanics have been enormous and are being replicated all over the industry. Currently, Axie boasts 2.8 million active players and $3.6 billion traded on their in-house marketplace.

ILV

Iluvium is another project that has risen to prominence through exploring the play-to-earn mechanics. Although far smaller than Axie Infinity, it is certainly not a negligible force: since launch in 2021 ILV rose from just a few million dollars in market cap to a high of well over $1 billion.

ENJ

Enjin, along Decentraland, is a project that has been focused on gaming and the metaverse for a while now (aeons in terms of some of the rest of the projects listed in $PLAY). As such, they have developed their product offerings and diversified the organisation. Nowadays, Enjin provides end-to-end solutions for launching and managing NFTs across a variety of spheres including art, music, sport, gaming, collectibles, etc. They are particularly focused on the ways in which companies can be helped to implement and integrate NFTs into their platforms in order to better interact with their customers and clients.

GALA

Gala Games is a company that is focused on building games that have blockchains implemented into them, and are focused on doing so in such a way that the blockchains are effectively invisible to the end user. This thesis of putting the UX first guides their operations: they want to use the benefits of blockchain (most notably verifiable ownership of assets within games) to enhance the gameplay experience. Thus far, they have built a wide variety of games that span various formats. In a further effort to decentralise the Gala ecosystem, participants are able to run their own nodes (there are currently over 16,000) for more benefits in terms of accrual of $GALA as well as exclusive NFTs.

AUDIO

Audius is a project focused on democratising the music industry through NFTs. Their business thesis is that the current state of artists producing music is too elitist and that the barriers are too high: signing with record labels isn’t an easy thing to do, and without it many musicians find themselves unable to gain the traction that they seek. For this reason, Audius has built a platform that allows artists to grow their communities and publish their music for free with no limitations or restrictions. They boast that they have the highest quality audio of any free streaming service. Their native token $AUDIO is used to govern the platform, reward the most popular artists, and to provide artists the ability to gate their music for exclusivity purposes.

YGG

Yield Guild Games is a community of gamers that collaborate together in play-to-earn games so that they are more profitable. As well as this, YGG invests in NFTs (particularly in-game assets such as virtual land) and makes them available for their members to borrow so that they can be used in-game. This thesis has made the P2E arena more efficient and made the industry far more profitable for many gamers.

The future of experience

The above projects represent a shift from the current state of gaming, in which those who play are consumers alone, to a more egalitarian form of gaming in which ecosystems are built that have the potential to become fully autonomous. This process is not confined to gaming alone, but metaverses also represent a future in which the physical world becomes less meaningful and the digital world more so. Lockdowns showed the world the importance of the digital world, the limitations of the physical one, and the importance of innovating to ensure that this digital world is as beneficial as it can be. Metaverses are not just restricted to games: as bandwidth constraints improve and become less burdensome, and as more people come to populate these worlds, enhanced user interfaces will dictate that the user experience is also improved. The possibilities for moving the human experience into a digital space are profound and nearly limitless: education, socialisation, gaming, work… most human experiences can be transposed into such a world, and the benefits of decentralised blockchains mean that users can retain digital sovereignty and not fall prey to a surveillance dystopia, since personal data can be retained.

The trends are clear: the space has exploded over the past couple of years. When it comes to finding the best way to invest in these projects, it is clear that diversification and risk management are responsible strategies, and the ability for PieDAO to automate and oversee the management of the $PLAY index means that potential investors and speculators are provided with all the tools they need to make passive investments. The unique structure of PieDAO means that there are also potential opportunities for meta-governance in the future across the future, and that either $DOUGH or $PLAY could be used to participate in a variety of different ecosystems simultaneously and seamlessly.

Since inception, $PLAY has performed extraordinarily, and has generated phenomenal returns for holders. All of PieDAO’s pies start at a value of $1, and at the time of writing $PLAY stands at $2.40. Indeed, from the lows of June to heights of November, $PLAY rose from approximately $0.50 to $7, a 14x return. The markets may be volatile, and indeed there have been huge swings in the price, but for long-term investors such volatility is par for the course. Those who have provided liquidity for $PLAY have also been extremely profitable: the launch of PieDAO’s DOUGHpamine programme to incentivise liquidity provision initially gave the SushiSwap PLAY/DOUGH LP an APR of 1500%, and even though more capital has headed in this direction, the yields still stand well above 100% .

With ETH Amsterdam on the horizon, there is no doubt that VC-fuelled chicanery, speculation, and investment will continue well into 2022. For those who have the knack to recognise the degen play du jour, there are plenty of profits to be made.

However, for those who are more interested in consolidating and building a long term, responsible portfolio, but who are also confident that the dematerialisation of the physical world is not only a burgeoning trend but a continuing one, $PLAY is a brilliant tool — particularly for those who subscribe to the maxim that “diversification is the only free lunch in investing”.
